correctness.rationale: Fix the submitted formula requiring both an a-opposite and a b-opposite successor. The recurrence gives R_i^t=R_i^0 ∩ (W×S_t) with common decreasing target set S_t. Initial reflexivity makes distinct S_t distinguishable by self-arrows, though the updated relations need not be reflexive. The at-most-two initial class size makes each opposite successor unique if present, and restriction of targets makes it available exactly while in S_t. Each color is a matching; a connected component of the two-color multigraph is an alternating path or cycle, including isolated singletons and the two-edge parallel cycle. Path endpoints fail the test, both-colored cycle vertices never fail, and applying this recursively gives exactly the claimed stages and first unchanged update. A single alternating path realizes the bound for every positive n, including n=1. On the fixed valuation propositional truths are invariant; on an initially S5 model atom-free static modal truth is constant across worlds by total atom-free bisimulation with serial relations. Thus either no arrows or all arrows are deleted by an atom-free first update, so both resource bounds hold. Independently replayed direct relation semantics on a mixed model with path, singleton components, a parallel cycle and an ordinary four-cycle; the component stages matched.
residual_risks: Correctness concerns the specified formula, not all one-atom formulas on this class. Finite corroboration is not used in place of the component proof.

evidence: Resultary 65b4b662c65e proves a sharp general |W| bound using a directed cycle on an arbitrary frame. The September paper’s Lemma 6 gives the single-agent K45 valuation-type bound; the sigma-validity theorem classifies sequence patterns across frame classes; Theorem 25 of arXiv:2611.11911 treats uniform boundedness versus eventual stabilization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These bounds and existence/pattern classifications do not give the exact per-model half-path duration or the surviving target sets. The general |W| bound cannot simply be halved on the same resource class.

evidence: The same-resource n-step formula requires only an a-opposite successor at true worlds or a b-opposite successor at false worlds. The assigned formula requires an opposite successor from BOTH agents at either truth value.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Removing the one-sided dependencies does not specialize its exact n-step path witness into a theorem about both-sided deletion on all components. The submitted half-world bound is formula-specific, not a resource-class maximum, and the unboundedness corollary alone is not the distinctive contribution.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported claim is the complete path/cycle target trace and exact half-world index for this fixed BOTH-partners formula on initial binary-cell two-agent S5. The strongest related records cover graph geometry, a general bound, a different fixed formula in the same resource class, or a different update. They do not give the trace for the submitted formula. No priority is claimed for the coarse resource boundary independently of that trace.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent pruning dynamics or an implicit construction elsewhere in the broader announcement literature remains possible. The one-atom/two-agent resource phenomenon overlaps the different formula in 3ec574a60e94; dates are not used to infer priority.

value.rationale: For the natural opposite-truth-witness rule, the theorem traces every target at every time, distinguishes permanently surviving cycles from transient paths, and gives exact time even for disconnected models. This is a structural semantics result, not just a large example or a general monotone deletion bound. It explains how a fixed tiny formula gives unbounded lifetimes even on binary S5 information cells without confusing the formula-specific constant with a maximum over all formulas.
residual_risks: The interpretation is specific to two matchings and this formula; no general bound for arbitrary information-cell sizes is implied.
